$comment: What the installer carries outside the crate and npm package graphs, for scripts/third-party-notices.ps1. Each entry was checked against the version in `tiedTo`; once the tree resolves another, the gate fails until the entry is checked again (see README.md). `markers` name the helper signatures (notices-lib.ps1) the built interface must show for the entry, and `texts` the folder here holding its license texts.

components.name: Vite runtime helpers (preload helper, __vite__mapDeps)
components.note: Emitted by Vite into the built interface: code for loading its chunks, not the build tool itself.

components.name: Vite module preload polyfill (adapted from es-module-shims)
components.note: Emitted by Vite into the built interface; its notice is Guy Bedford's, as the source carries it.

components.name: CommonJS interop helper (@rollup/plugin-commonjs, bundled in Vite)
components.note: Emitted into the built interface for the CommonJS packages it bundles (React among them).

components.name: NSIS (the installer's stub, its LZMA decompressor and the NSISdl plug-in)
components.source: https://github.com/kichik/nsis/tree/v311 (Debian trixie's nsis package, in docker/windows-build.Dockerfile)
components.note: setup.exe is built with NSIS and carries its runtime code; the zlib/libpng license covers NSIS itself and the Common Public License its LZMA module, as COPYING says.

components.name: nsis_tauri_utils.dll
components.note: An NSIS plug-in that Tauri's bundler embeds in setup.exe. It is built with windows-sys, whose license texts are among the crates above.

components.name: WebView2 loader (WebView2LoaderStatic.lib, Microsoft.Web.WebView2 SDK)
components.note: Linked statically into luna.exe through webview2-com-sys, which ships the SDK's library byte for byte. The WebView2 runtime itself is not shipped: the installer downloads Microsoft's Evergreen bootstrapper when the runtime is missing, under Microsoft's own terms.

components.name: Microsoft Visual C++ runtime (vcruntime, static library)
components.license: Microsoft Visual Studio license terms, Distributable Code
components.note: Linked statically into luna.exe (static_vcruntime, through tauri-build); the Universal CRT it links dynamically is part of Windows. The runtime libraries are Distributable Code under the Visual Studio license terms (https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/license-terms/; the list at https://learn.microsoft.com/visualstudio/releases/2022/redistribution), distributed here on the conditions those terms set.
components.noText: Microsoft publishes the terms, not a license text to reproduce; they are linked above.
